name: Norm AI
subsector: Agentic law, regulatory compliance and supervised legal services
product: Builds attorney-engineered legal and compliance agents, an inline supervisory layer for enterprise AI, and supplies the technology used by affiliated AI-native law firm Norm Law.
targetCustomer: Regulated financial institutions, asset managers, insurers and large enterprises
buyer: General counsel, chief compliance officer, chief risk officer or enterprise AI governance leader
latestRound: $120M Series C at a $1.2B valuation, Jul 2026
traction: Norm reports clients representing more than $30T in aggregate assets under management; this is client AUM, not Norm revenue, and the number of clients and ARR are not disclosed.
notes: This is materially broader than a generic legal copilot: Norm combines a regulatory domain-specific language, attorney-built agents, legal-reasoning research, API/MCP/OpenTelemetry supervision and an affiliated law firm with outcome-based pricing. The law-firm feedback loop and embedded legal expertise are plausible moats, but regulated-service delivery, conflicts, human review and margins are structural constraints. Funding is a company-reported lower bound (> $260M). LinkedIn exposed roughly 204-205 associated profiles while its configured company-size band still showed 51-200; the atlas therefore stores the profile-derived 201-500 range with lower confidence than the other fields.

name: Tangos AI
subsector: Autonomous financial-crime, sanctions and risk investigations
product: Runs end-to-end AML, sanctions, fraud, enhanced-due-diligence and intelligence investigations from an escalated alert to a source-traced, examiner-ready case file.
targetCustomer: Banks, fintechs, payment providers, government agencies and intelligence organizations
buyer: Chief compliance officer, MLRO, head of financial-crime investigations or government intelligence leader
traction: The company says it is already supporting major financial institutions and intelligence organizations; its LinkedIn page more specifically says it is in production with a major U.S. fintech and international intelligence organizations, but customers, contract values and independently measured accuracy are not public.
notes: Tangos is not primarily another detection or alert-scoring product: its wedge is the expensive L2/L3 investigation work after an alert, using expert playbooks, hypothesis testing, counter-evidence, provenance and immutable audit trails. It supports cloud, private-cloud and air-gapped deployment and proposes proof-of-value comparisons on historical cases. That creates strong métier integration; the technical moat remains unproven until accuracy, false-positive/negative rates and production references can be independently audited. Funding and traction were announced only in Jul 2026, and most evidence is company-issued.

name: Aligned
hq: New York, USA and Tel Aviv, Israel
subsector: AI-native B2B deal execution and digital sales rooms
product: Provides a shared buyer-seller deal workspace in which AI agents build deal rooms and assets, map stakeholders, interpret intent and risk, answer buyer questions and recommend or execute next steps.
targetCustomer: B2B sales, revenue operations and customer-success teams running complex deals
buyer: Chief revenue officer, VP Sales, head of revenue operations or customer-success leader
traction: Aligned reports 70,000 sellers and 1M monthly buyers, customers including Deel, Similarweb and WordPress, and 3x ARR growth over the prior 12 months; the company does not disclose ARR, retention or customer concentration.
notes: The strongest moat thesis is not a novel base model but ownership of the buyer-facing transaction surface and its between-meeting activity data across calls, email, CRM and workspace engagement. This is meaningful workflow/data differentiation, though sales-tech competition is intense and the AI stack is not technically disclosed enough to establish model-level IP. The company release inconsistently refers to 70,000 sellers in its body and over 70,000 revenue teams in its boilerplate; this entry uses the narrower, internally consistent seller metric. CTech reported 55 employees and a small secondary component in the Series B; funding is recorded at the announced financing total without attempting to split that component.

name: LinqAlpha
subsector: AI-native institutional investment and global-markets research
product: Provides institutional investors with specialized AI agents that connect market, filings, web and internal data, learn each team's investment framework and produce source-linked multi-step research across global public markets.
targetCustomer: Hedge funds, asset managers, investment banks and institutional public-markets teams
buyer: Head of investment research, CIO, portfolio manager or head of sell-side research and trading
fundingDisplay: $28.6M disclosed funding, derived from a $6.6M seed plus $22M Series A
traction: LinqAlpha reports more than 70 financial-institution clients across the U.S., Europe and Asia, including Causeway Capital Management and Schonfeld, with its buy-side customers managing more than $5T in aggregate assets; a founder separately reported 30% month-over-month growth, but ARR is not disclosed.
notes: The initial user label is accurate but underspecified: LinqAlpha is vertical institutional-finance software, not a generic web research assistant. Its technical differentiation includes finance-specific retrieval and embedding research, multilingual/global source coverage, cross-model delegation and fully source-linked outputs; its business integration spans market data, filings, internal documents and reusable analyst workflows. The moat is not yet proven against Bloomberg, FactSet, AlphaSense and bank-built tooling because LinqAlpha licenses or connects much of the underlying data and has only 70+ disclosed institutions. The $28.6M total is an arithmetic sum of two separately announced equity rounds, not a company-stated lifetime total.
